examples.en: My father studied abroad during his young adulthood.

examples.ko: 청년기에 겪은 경험이 평생 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Experiences in young adulthood affect you for life.
Most people worry a lot about their career path in young adulthood.
That writer spent his youth abroad.
Health habits from young adulthood carry into old age.
It's fascinating to hear stories of my grandfather's youth.

examples.ko: 청년기와 장년기는 몸 상태가 많이 달라요.
examples.en: Physical condition is very different in young adulthood and middle age.

explain: 사람의 삶을 나눌 때 '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'처럼 나오는 시기 이름이에요. 청소년기 다음, 어른이 되어 가는 시기를 말해요. 글이나 수업에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I spent my young adulthood abroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시기를 어떻게 살았는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how one lived through that stage.

phrases.en: Worries in young adulthood are mostly about career and love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시기에 겪는 걱정과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with worries typical of this age.

phrases.en: At twenty you enter young adulthood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 시기가 시작될 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Marks the beginning of a new life stage.

explain_en: Neutral term for the life stage of young adulthood, in writing. This is a life-stage name seen in lists like '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'. It means the period after the teen years, when one becomes an adult. You often see it in texts and lessons.

examples.en: Even after marriage, I call my father often.
My father sent me kimchi.
My father farms in the countryside.
It's my father's birthday, so I'm going down this weekend.
I'm tall because I take after my father.
I left my child with my father and went to work.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 아버지를 말할 때 써요. 남편의 아버지는 '시아버지', 남자가 아내의 아버지를 말할 때는 '장인어른'이라고 해요. 결혼 전의 딸이 말할 때는 그냥 '아버지'를 써요.

phrases.en: I called my father to ask how he's doing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높임 조사 '께'를 붙여 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the honorific particle 께 to be respectful.

phrases.en: My father is coming tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높임말 '-시-'를 붙여 아버지의 행동을 높일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the honorific -시- to show respect to the father.

phrases.en: My dad is good at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친정아버지보다 가깝고 편한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warmer, more casual way than 친정아버지.

explain_en: A married woman uses this for her own father. Her husband's father is '시아버지', and a man calls his wife's father '장인어른'. An unmarried daughter would simply say '아버지'.

examples.ko: 그 커플은 결혼식 한 달 전에 파혼했어요.
examples.en: That couple broke off their engagement a month before the wedding.
Our values were too different, so we decided to call off the engagement.
I heard the news that my friend suddenly broke off her engagement.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 두 사람은 오해 때문에 파혼해요.
examples.en: In the drama, the two break off their engagement because of a misunderstanding.
If you break off the engagement, what happens to the wedding hall fee?
We almost broke off the engagement because of my parents' objection.

explain: 약혼이나 결혼 약속을 깼을 때 써요. 이미 결혼한 사이가 헤어지는 것은 '이혼하다'라고 해요. 한 사람이 일방적으로 깰 때는 '파혼을 통보하다'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.en: The two of them broke off their engagement because of circumstances.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파혼하다'를 과거형으로 쓴 말이에요. 이미 끝난 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form of '파혼하다', for something already over.

phrases.en: He suddenly announced the end of the engagement by text.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한쪽이 일방적으로 알릴 때 써요. 조금 무거운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one side announces it unilaterally. It sounds rather heavy.

phrases.example: 가족 반대 때문에 파혼하게 됐다고 들었어요.
phrases.en: I heard they ended up breaking off the engagement because of family opposition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어쩔 수 없는 상황 때문에 그렇게 되었다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries the feeling that it happened because of circumstances beyond one's control.
phrases.en_equiv: to end up breaking the engagement

explain_en: Use it when an engagement or a promise to marry is broken. For couples already married, the word is '이혼하다' (divorce). When one side does it alone, people say '파혼을 통보하다' (announce the break-off).

en: to reconcile; to settle; to compromise

examples.en: I made up with the friend I fought with yesterday.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 화해하는 장면에서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried at the scene where the two people make up.
I want to apologize first and make up with my younger sibling.

examples.ko: 사이가 나빴던 두 나라가 화해해서 다시 무역을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The two countries that had been on bad terms reconciled and started trading again.
Shall we make up now?

examples.ko: 부모님과 화해하려면 먼저 마음을 열어야 해요.
examples.en: To make up with your parents, you first have to open your heart.

explain: 싸운 뒤에 다시 사이가 좋아질 때 써요. 한쪽이 사과하고 다른 쪽이 받아 주면 화해하게 돼요. 'A와 화해하다'처럼 '와/과'와 같이 써요. 반대는 '다투다'예요. 가볍게는 '마음을 풀다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The two friends made up with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 붙여 둘 다 마음을 푼다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 서로 gives a sense that both sides let go of the conflict.
phrases.en_equiv: to make up with each other

phrases.en: I told my younger sibling first, 'Let's make up.'
phrases.nuance_ko: '-자'는 반말로 화해를 청할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -자 ending is a casual form used to propose making up.

phrases.en: After hearing the apology, my friend let go of the anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화해보다 가볍게, 화난 마음을 푼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter way to say letting go of one's anger.
phrases.en_equiv: to let go of one's anger

explain_en: Use it when people become friendly again after a fight. It happens when one side apologizes and the other accepts. It goes with the particle 와/과, as in 'A와 화해하다'. The opposite is 다투다. In a lighter way people also say '마음을 풀다'.

examples.en: I submitted the draft plan to the team leader.
The new plan is much more specific than the last one.
I will explain the draft plan at the meeting.
The budget is missing from the draft plan.
The draft plan I wrote was approved.

examples.ko: 계획안을 한 번 더 고쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Please revise the draft plan one more time.

explain: '계획'은 마음속 생각이나 일정 전체를 말하고, 계획안은 종이나 파일에 적은 '문서'예요. 회사나 학교에서 제출하고 검토하는 글에 써요. '계획서'와 거의 같지만 계획안은 아직 확정 전이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I wrote up a new draft plan on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서로 계획을 쓸 때 '작성하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 작성하다 for writing a plan as a document.

phrases.en: The team leader is reviewing the draft plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제출한 뒤 읽고 확인하는 단계에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone reads and checks a submitted plan.

phrases.en: I have to submit the plan by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획안과 거의 같지만 확정된 문서라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same, but feels more final than 계획안.

explain_en: Proposed plan or lesson outline, not yet final. 계획 can be a thought or a whole schedule, while 계획안 is a written document. It is used in companies and schools for something you submit and review. It is close to 계획서, but 계획안 feels not yet final.

examples.en: I study education at university.
I have an education class this afternoon.
My sister majored in education.
Education textbooks are not as hard as I thought.
To become a teacher, you need to know education theory too.
That person is a professor of education.

explain: '교육'은 가르치고 배우는 일이고, 교육학은 그것을 연구하는 학문 이름이에요. 대학에는 '교육학과'가 있고, 교사가 되려는 사람이 많이 공부해요. '경제학', '심리학'처럼 '-학'이 붙은 말과 함께 묶어서 외우면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling attends the education department at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 교육학을 가르치는 학과 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the university department that teaches education.

phrases.en: I'm majoring in education to become a teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 주로 공부하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which field one mainly studies at university.

phrases.en: That education scholar studies children's play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육학을 연구하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who studies education as a field.

explain_en: '교육' is the act of teaching and learning, while 교육학 is the name of the academic field that studies it. Universities have a '교육학과' (department of education), and many people who want to become teachers study it. It is easy to remember together with other '-학' words like '경제학' and '심리학'.

en: to be selected; to be chosen; to be designated

examples.en: My essay was selected as the best entry.
I'm glad I was chosen employee of the month.

examples.ko: 후보 중에서 한 명이 선정될 거예요.
examples.en: One of the candidates will be selected.
We text the people who were selected.
It was chosen as this year's best movie.
I'm sorry I wasn't selected in the review.

explain: '뽑히다'는 입말, '선정되다'는 심사나 기준을 거쳐 공식적으로 뽑힌다는 느낌이에요. 공모전·장학금·상 이야기에 자주 나와요. 고르는 쪽은 '선정하다'예요.

phrases.en: I was chosen as the class representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입말에서 더 자연스럽고 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter word that is more natural in speech.

phrases.en: That movie was selected as a candidate for the award.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~로'를 붙여 어떤 자격으로 뽑혔는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~로' to say in what role someone was chosen.
phrases.en_equiv: to be selected as a candidate

phrases.en: Unfortunately, I wasn't selected this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심사에서 떨어졌을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone did not pass a selection.

explain_en: Passive; chosen after review — prizes, sites, winners; formal. '뽑히다' is spoken style; '선정되다' implies being chosen officially after a review or criteria. Common for contests, scholarships and awards. The choosing side is '선정하다'.

dis.h: chosen after review; prizes, sites, winners
gh: picked via exam or competition; team, staff
picked from many for a key role

p.n: 선발되다 suggests being picked through a test or competition; 선정되다 is a general choice after review.

t90.ax: We text the people who were selected.

examples.en: My older sister studies pharmacy at university.

examples.ko: 약학과에 가려면 공부를 정말 많이 해야 해요.
examples.en: To get into the pharmacy department you have to study a lot.

examples.ko: 약학 수업에서 약이 몸에서 어떻게 작용하는지 배웠어요.
examples.en: In pharmacy class we learned how drugs work in the body.

examples.ko: 그분은 약학 박사 학위가 있는 연구원이에요.
examples.en: That person is a researcher with a doctorate in pharmacy.

examples.ko: 약학을 졸업하면 약사 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: After graduating in pharmacy, you can take the pharmacist exam.

examples.ko: 약학과 의학은 비슷하지만 다루는 부분이 달라요.
examples.en: Pharmacy and medicine are similar, but they handle different areas.

explain: 약을 연구하고 만드는 방법을 공부하는 학문이에요. 약을 파는 사람은 '약사', 가게는 '약국'이라고 구분해요. 의사가 병을 고치고 처방하는 사람이라면, 약학은 약 자체를 다루는 공부예요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is in the pharmacy department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교의 학과 이름으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the name of a university department.

phrases.en: I want to major in pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 무엇을 공부하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what you study at university.

phrases.en: Studying pharmacy involves a lot of memorizing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부하는 일 자체를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the studying itself.

explain_en: It is the field that studies drugs and how to make them. The person who sells medicine is 약사 and the shop is 약국. A doctor treats illness and prescribes; 약학 deals with the drug itself.

t90.ax: My older sister studies pharmacy at university.

en: to drop out of school; to leave school voluntarily; to give up school willingly

examples.en: My older brother dropped out of school last year.
That friend left school and is preparing for the equivalency exam.
Talk with your teacher before you drop out.

examples.ko: 정말 자퇴할 거예요? 부모님은 알고 계세요?
examples.en: Are you really going to drop out? Do your parents know?
I had to leave school because I was sick.

examples.ko: 자퇴한 학생도 다시 입학할 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can a student who dropped out enroll again?

explain: 스스로 그만두면 '자퇴', 학교가 내보내면 '퇴학'이에요. 일상에서는 '학교를 그만두다'라고 해도 되지만, 서류에서는 '자퇴서를 내다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I submitted a withdrawal form to my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교를 그만둘 때 내는 서류와 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with the document you submit to leave school.

phrases.en: My older brother quit school last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '자퇴하다' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 'drop out.'

phrases.en: Studying is so hard that I want to drop out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바라는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 싶다' expresses a wish.

explain_en: Leaving by your own choice is 자퇴, while being sent away by the school is 퇴학. In daily talk you can say '학교를 그만두다', but on paperwork it is '자퇴서를 내다' (submit a withdrawal form).

examples.en: The diver slowly went down into the sea.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 십 년째 잠수부로 일하고 계세요.
examples.en: My uncle has worked as a diver for ten years.
Divers are examining the sunken ship.
A diver goes into the water carrying an oxygen tank.
When I was little, my dream was to be a diver.

examples.ko: 구조 현장에 잠수부를 열 명 더 보냈어요.
examples.en: They sent ten more divers to the rescue site.

explain: 일이나 구조 작업으로 물속에 들어가는 사람을 말할 때 자주 써요. 취미로 스쿠버 다이빙을 하는 사람은 '다이버'라고도 많이 불러요.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 다이버라서 바다 이야기를 많이 알아요.
phrases.en: My friend is a diver, so he knows a lot about the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미로 즐기는 사람에게 더 많이 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word used more for people who dive as a hobby.

phrases.en: My uncle works as a diver at the port.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업으로 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when diving is someone's job.

phrases.en: A rescue diver found the person underwater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 구조 상황에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in accident and rescue situations.

explain_en: It is commonly used for people who go underwater for work or rescue operations. People who scuba dive as a hobby are also often called '다이버'.

examples.en: He dropped out of university and started a business.
I dropped out of high school because of family circumstances.

examples.ko: 중퇴한 학생들이 다시 공부하는 학교가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a school where students who dropped out study again.
I worried for a long time about whether to drop out.
My friend is dropping out in order to work.
Many people succeeded even after dropping out of college.

explain: 학교를 졸업하기 전에 중간에 그만둘 때 쓰고, '대학을 중퇴하다'처럼 학교 이름 뒤에 '을/를'을 붙여요. 반대말은 '졸업하다'예요. 잠깐 쉬는 '휴학하다'와 달리 학교를 아예 그만두는 거예요.

phrases.en: I quit school because I was sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 입말로 '중퇴하다'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 졸업 전이라는 느낌은 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple spoken alternative, though it doesn't stress leaving before graduation as much.

phrases.example: 대학교를 중퇴한 사람도 성공할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: People who dropped out of university can succeed too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄴ'을 붙여 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -(으)ㄴ ending describes a person who has dropped out.

phrases.en: Even if it's hard, I won't drop out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교를 계속 다니겠다는 결심을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express a decision to keep attending school.

explain_en: It is used when you leave school partway, before graduating, and you attach 을/를 to the school: '대학을 중퇴하다'. The opposite is '졸업하다'. Unlike '휴학하다', which is taking a break, 중퇴하다 means leaving school for good.

en: to be eliminated; to fail; to be knocked out

examples.en: Our team was eliminated in the first match.
I cried a lot because I failed the audition.

examples.ko: 서류 심사에서 탈락하면 면접을 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you are cut at the document screening, you cannot have an interview.
The people who were eliminated will also get a message.
I prepared hard so as not to be eliminated this time.

examples.ko: 저는 오디션 프로그램에서 탈락할 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not expect to be eliminated from the audition show.

explain: '탈락하다'는 대회나 시험, 오디션에서 다음 단계로 못 가고 떨어진다는 말이에요. '떨어지다'는 시험 전체에 쓰고, '탈락하다'는 여러 단계 중 한 곳에서 빠질 때 더 잘 어울려요. 반대로 통과하면 '합격하다', '통과하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was eliminated in the first round of screening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정을 받아서 빠진다는 느낌의 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form with the feel of being removed by a decision.

phrases.en: The list of those eliminated will be announced tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단계에서 떨어진 사람을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a person who was eliminated at a stage.

phrases.en: Luckily, I wasn't eliminated this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다음 단계로 간 일을 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when you advanced to the next stage.

explain_en: Intransitive: one fails a test or round (시험에서 탈락하다) 탈락하다 means failing to move on to the next stage of a contest, exam or audition. 떨어지다 works for a whole exam, while 탈락하다 fits better when you drop out at one of several stages. When you pass, the words are 합격하다 and 통과하다.

t90.ax: Our team was eliminated in the first match.

examples.en: The kids leave school at three in the afternoon.
It rained, so I went home from school with my friend.
I stopped by a convenience store on my way home from school.

examples.ko: 동생이 하교하면 같이 저녁을 먹을 거예요.
examples.en: When my younger sibling gets home from school, we'll have dinner together.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 학생들이 평소보다 일찍 하교해요.
examples.en: During exam week, students leave school earlier than usual.

examples.ko: 하교하고 바로 학원에 가야 해서 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have to go straight to a cram school after school, so it's tiring.

explain: 반대말은 '등교하다'예요. '하교 시간', '하굣길'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 학생에게만 쓰고, 회사에서 집으로 갈 때는 '퇴근하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The area in front of the school is crowded at dismissal time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생들이 학교에서 나오는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time students leave school.

phrases.en: I ate tteokbokki with a friend on the way home from school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 집으로 가는 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the way from school back home.

phrases.en: After school, I go to a cram school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 말할 때 '-고 나서'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 나서' to talk about order of events.

explain_en: The opposite is '등교하다'. It also appears in nouns such as '하교 시간' and '하굣길'. It is only for students; leaving work is '퇴근하다'.
